from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Visualization", ["A sphere casts a circular shadow.", "The shadow's radius matches the sphere's.", "Light rays project this circular shape."])
        
        # Define objects
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        # Using 3DScene principles for sphere/cylinder visualization
        cylinder = Cylinder(radius=1, height=2, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        radius_line = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT, color="#FF0000")
        radius_label = Text("R", color="#FF0000", font_size=24)
        
        height_line = Line(UP, DOWN, color="#00FFFF")
        height_label = Text("2R", color="#00FFFF", font_size=24)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(cylinder), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.place_at_grid(radius_line, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(radius_label, "B4")
        self.play(Create(radius_line), Write(radius_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(height_line, "E5")
        self.place_at_grid(height_label, "E6")
        self.play(Create(height_line), Write(height_label), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(sphere.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Sphere area equals four circle areas.",
            "The ratio is exactly four to one.",
            "Unwrapping the sphere fills four discs.",
            "Formula: sphere surface area is 4πr².",
            "Formula: shadow area is πr²."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Geometric Relationship", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialize objects
        formula1 = MathTex(r"A_{sphere} = 4\pi r^2", font_size=36, color="#FF0000")
        formula2 = MathTex(r"A_{cylinder\_side} = 2\pi r h", font_size=36, color="#00FFFF")
        formula3 = MathTex(r"h = 2r \implies A = 4\pi r^2", font_size=36, color="#FFFFFF")
        
        # Position them

        self.place_at_grid(formula2, "D2")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A sphere fits inside a cylinder.",
            "Their surface areas are remarkably equal.",
            "This is Archimedes' Hat-Box Theorem.",
            "Curvature distributes area to cylinder walls.",
            "Area calculation is simplified by this."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Archimedes' Hat-Box Theorem", lecture_lines)
        
        # Geometry setup
        radius = 1.0
        sphere = Sphere(radius=radius, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        cylinder = Cylinder(radius=radius, height=2*radius, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        # Placeholder for animations
        sphere_cap = Circle(radius=radius, color="#FF9900", fill_opacity=0.8).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        
        # Ensure we don't block C3/D3
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'C5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(cylinder, 'C5', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(sphere), Create(cylinder))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF9900"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        label = Text("Archimedes Hat-Box", font_size=24, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'A4')
        self.play(Write(label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#99FF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Spheres are nature's efficient shapes.", "They minimize surface area for volume.", "This concept helps conserve animal heat."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Review key area formula comparison
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.8, color=BLUE).set_opacity(0.5)
        formula = MathTex("4\\pi r^2 \\text{ vs } \\pi r^2").set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'B3')
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3')
        self.play(Create(sphere), Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show Earth map projection example
        projection = Circle(radius=0.6, color="#00FFFF")
        projection_label = Text("Minimal Area", font_size=18, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(projection, 'B5')
        self.place_at_grid(projection_label, 'C5')
        self.play(Create(projection), Write(projection_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final summary text appears
        summary = Text("Efficiency = Heat Conservation", font_size=24, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(summary, 'E5')
        self.play(FadeIn(summary))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometric Bridge: Sphere Surface Area and Its Projected Shadow

sections.title: Prerequisite Visualization (1 min)
sections.content: Establish the definition of a sphere and its orthogonal projection. Define parallel light rays striking a sphere to create a circular shadow. Explain that the radius of the projected circle is identical to the radius (r) of the sphere.
sections.example: Visualize a basketball under a bright noon sun casting a circular shadow on the court.

sections.title: The Core Geometric Relationship (1.5 min)
sections.content: Introduce the formula for the surface area of a sphere (A = 4πr²) and the area of its projected shadow (A_shadow = πr²). Highlight the constant ratio of 4:1 using a split-screen animation showing the sphere surface being 'unwrapped' to fill exactly four shadow-sized discs.
sections.example: Imagine a flexible, paper-like membrane covering the sphere; show it being peeled off and cut into four perfect circles, each matching the size of the shadow.

sections.title: Archimedes' Hat-Box Theorem (1.5 min)
sections.content: Explain that the surface area of a sphere is equal to the lateral surface area of a circumscribed cylinder. Use a graphical overlay where the sphere is inscribed in a cylinder of height 2r, illustrating how the curvature of the sphere distributes area identically to the cylinder's walls.
sections.example: A spherical robot character ('Orbito') fitting perfectly inside a cylindrical charging station; the surface area of the robot is mathematically equal to the inner wall area of the cylinder.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application (1 min)
sections.content: Recap the 4πr² vs πr² relationship. Connect this to light intensity (inverse square law) or heat dissipation. Explain why spheres are nature’s most efficient shape for minimizing surface area relative to volume.
sections.example: A polar bear curling into a ball (sphere-like) to minimize heat loss; compare the effective 'shadow' area of its body to its total surface area to explain heat conservation.
